note: Rules the business finder follows, each with the page it comes from. Re-check the sources before changing any number here.

rules.rule: Commercial email, including business to business, needs honest header and subject lines, must say it is an ad or about your services, must include a valid physical postal address, must tell people how to opt out, and opt-outs must be honored within 10 business days. The sender is responsible even when someone else sends it.
rules.how_we_follow_it: Every email draft carries the member's mailing address (or a placeholder to fill in) and a P.S. that says it is about their services with a reply-to-opt-out line. Drafts are sent by the member, one at a time.

rules.topic: Texts and calls to cell phones (US)
rules.rule: Autodialed or prerecorded calls and texts to wireless numbers need the person's prior consent.
rules.how_we_follow_it: No cold text drafts. Calls are made by hand from the call sheet.

rules.rule: Instagram's Terms of Use don't allow collecting information in an automated way or accessing the service through unauthorized automated means.
rules.how_we_follow_it: We never read Instagram. DMs are drafts the member sends by hand; the Instagram handle comes from the business's own website.

rules.rule: Places API content must not be pre-fetched, cached or stored beyond the allowed exceptions; the place ID is exempt from the caching restrictions. Attributions for place details must be shown.
rules.how_we_follow_it: Google results are never cached. CSVs, the Pipeline and saved files keep only the place ID, a Maps link built from it, and facts read off the business's own website. Run views that show Places data say Google Maps.

rules.rule: Up to 20 results a page, a nextPageToken for more, 60 results at most for one search.
rules.how_we_follow_it: One search pulls up to 3 pages.

rules.topic: Google Places cost (our cost, not the member's)
rules.rule: Text Search Enterprise: $35 per 1,000 requests with 1,000 free a month. A request bills at the highest tier of any field it asks for; website, phone and rating are Enterprise fields.
rules.how_we_follow_it: A search is 1 to 3 requests, about $0.04 to $0.11 of our cost, priced at 8 credits.

rules.rule: Place Details returns at most 5 reviews, sorted by relevance, and the reviews field bills at the Enterprise + Atmosphere tier. Review authors must be credited wherever reviews are shown.
rules.how_we_follow_it: The business finder and competitor intel never pull Google review text. Ratings and review counts are used only to rank inside a run and never appear in messages or exports.

rules.topic: Finding a city on the map (OpenStreetMap Nominatim)
rules.rule: At most 1 request a second, an identifying User-Agent, cache results, and show attribution.
rules.how_we_follow_it: One request at a time with a pause, results cached for 30 days, and every OpenStreetMap list says (c) OpenStreetMap contributors.

rules.rule: OpenStreetMap data is open data under the ODbL; credit "(c) OpenStreetMap contributors".
rules.how_we_follow_it: Lists and files from OpenStreetMap carry the credit.

rules.rule: Maps URLs open Google Maps with a search (query and query_place_id) or directions (origin, destination, travelmode, waypoints) without an API key. Up to three waypoints are supported on mobile browsers and nine otherwise; each waypoint can be a place name, an address or latitude,longitude. Page last updated 2026-10-16, read 2026-10-19.
rules.how_we_follow_it: Map links for Google listings use the place ID. Walk-in routes are split into legs of up to 4 stops (3 waypoints and the destination) built from OpenStreetMap coordinates, so every leg opens on a phone; each stop's own map link goes to OpenStreetMap.

rules.rule: Yelp and Foursquare data isn't used for outreach (library rule, BUILDING.md).
rules.source: BUILDING.md, Harness engine and new rules

send_rules: Before you send, open their website and check every line is still true.
Send each one yourself, one at a time. No bulk DMs or auto-senders.
Email: keep your mailing address and the opt-out line. If they say no, stop and don't email again.
Don't cold-text a cell number. Call, email, DM or walk in.
Follow up on day 3 and day 7, then stop. Mark replies in your Pipeline.
